content.title: About
content.content: Plain microwave popcorn is a ready‑to‑cook snack that expands in a microwave oven. The bag contains dried corn kernels that pop quickly when heated, forming light, airy pieces. The flavor is neutral, without added salt or seasonings, making it a versatile base for further topping.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Popcorn is one of the few corn varieties whose kernels “explode” due to high internal moisture when heated.
The first commercial microwave popcorn appeared in the United States in the 1980s.
Plain microwave popcorn is relatively low‑calorie: about 350 kcal per 100 g of popped product.
Unlike traditional stovetop popcorn, microwave bags often contain a small amount of oil and stabilizers to ensure even popping.

items.title: Low in added fat
items.content: Plain microwave popcorn contains little to no added oil, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Corn kernels are rich in dietary fiber, which supports digestive health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Popcorn provides polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Quick source of glucose
items.content: The carbohydrates in popcorn are rapidly digestible, offering a fast energy boost.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Corn is naturally gluten‑free, so popcorn is safe for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to corn, experiencing skin or gastrointestinal reactions.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Popcorn can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Burn hazard
items.content: Steam inside the bag becomes very hot; open it carefully to avoid burns.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Certain brands add preservatives or flavor enhancers; choose a product with minimal additives if you have a sensitive stomach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Place the bag in the microwave, unfolding it according to the instructions. Cook on high power for 2–3 minutes, stopping when the interval between pops exceeds 2 seconds. Let the bag stand for a minute, then open, stir gently, and optionally season with salt, herbs, or cheese powder.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened bag in a cool, dry place away from moisture. After opening, transfer remaining kernels to an airtight container to maintain their popping ability.
